q1_issues.issue: The concessive's second argument is the family ENTITY sk_family_1, not a reified "being in the same language family" eventuality, so the connective relates a state to a thing instead of to the subordinate clause the rule requires.

The reified `related` state duplicates the fact already carried by the Related/Symmetric pair, and carries two Experiencer atoms for one state — a shape the instruction set never licenses (it routes stative symmetric predicates to relation + Symmetric tag and nothing else).

q2_gaps: a connective endpoint whose subordinate clause is a non-finite membership/locative state ("Despite BEING IN the same language family") — the copular-endpoint reification rule covers (Member subj prop) states but not a relational "be in X" clause, so there is no defined eventuality for the Despite atom to point at

a Symmetric-tagged stative relation as the anchor for a focus particle or a connective — the relation form is not an eventuality, and the focus/connective reification rules assume a one-place (Member subj prop) predication, leaving a two-participant state's reification (two Experiencers?) undefined
a degree adverb on a relational predicate ("only distantly related") — Manner is for event adverbs and Degree takes a single bearer, so a scalar adverb over a two-place relation has no slot
notes: The sameness of the family is well captured (one witness, both languages PartOf it) and Despite/Related/Symmetric/Only are all licensed heads; the failure is where the concessive's subordinate endpoint attaches. The parse omits kind typing for hungarian/finnish, which is correct — the text never states they are languages.
